rfm_tuples.R: 'Service Requests 17,184 [2024] 23,255 [2023] (6,071) (26)% ... Monetized Transactions 24,381 27,111 (2,730) (10)% ... Transacting Pros 168 196 (28) (14)%' — MD&A operating metrics table (Mode A read from filing).
rfm_tuples.f: Verify the disclosed metrics are consistent and that the framing matches the directional reality. Mode B: derive whether the multi-year trajectory is hidden by lopsided framing (e.g. claiming 'improved marketing efficiencies, Monetized Transactions per Service Request increased' to drape a 26% volume collapse).
rfm_tuples.M_value: Top-of-funnel collapse: Service Requests -26% YoY (17.18M vs 23.26M), Transacting Pros -14% (168k vs 196k), Domestic revenue -15% ($1.056B vs $1.243B). Three-year trajectory: Total revenue $1.185B (2024) vs $1.359B (2023) vs implied ~$1.764B (2022 prior to net-basis reclass — Services alone went from $381M gross-basis 2022 to $118M 2023 to $94M 2024). Marketplace fundamentally shrinking on every operational metric; the only positive metric ('Monetized Transactions per Service Request') is a denominator-shrink artifact. Note: Domestic revenue 2022 $1.663B → 2023 $1.243B → 2024 $1.056B — a 37% peak-to-current decline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is technically truthful but the framing ('user-experience enhancements', 'improved marketing efficiencies') euphemizes a >25% YoY collapse in the marketplace's primary leading indicator (Service Requests). For a two-sided marketplace, a -26% top-of-funnel and -14% supply (Pros) is consistent with network-effect erosion that compounds, not stabilizes.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The decrease in membership subscription revenue [-18%, -$9.2M] was primarily due to a decrease in professionals in the Angi network.' '...resulting in both lower Service Requests and lower acquisition of new professionals.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: filing acknowledges Pros are leaving. Mode B: management should disclose churn or net-pro adds if the trend were stabilizing; absence of any churn/cohort/retention metric is itself a Mode B signal in a marketplace that historically led with Pro counts.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + claim_evolution (no 10-K/proxy quantification of Pro retention disclosed)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Filing discloses Pro count is falling (Transacting Pros 196k→168k, membership subscription revenue -18%) but provides NO cohort, churn, or LTV disclosure. Prior Angi/IAC disclosures historically emphasized Pro growth as the core supply-side KPI. Mode B finding: when a marketplace stops disclosing supply-side cohort retention and pivots framing to 'monetization efficiency', that is consistent with a deteriorating supply side that management cannot positively frame.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Disclosure is candid that Pros are leaving but conspicuously lacks the cohort/retention metrics that would let an investor distinguish 'transient churn from cost discipline' vs 'platform abandonment'. The omission is itself informative for a marketplace.

rfm_tuples.R: 'On January 13, 2025, IAC announced that its board of directors approved a plan to spin off its full stake in the Company to IAC stockholders.' 'As of December 31, 2024, IAC's economic and voting interest in Angi were 85.3% and 98.3%, respectively.' Tax-sharing agreement 'imposes certain restrictions on us and our subsidiaries during the two (2) year p[eriod].'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: confirm spin announced. Mode B: derive what else must be true (1) ANGI faces a two-year tax-sharing restriction on M&A/capital structure that constrains strategic optionality precisely when the marketplace is shrinking; (2) the controlled-company governance was a crutch (IAC absorbed corporate overhead, talent, legal); (3) Joey Levin transition (5M Class B → personal Class A; 3M IAC RSA forfeited, $10.2M SBC reversal) signals the spin is being executed concurrently with senior leadership disengagement at the parent.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Spin will leave a shrinking, ~$1.18B revenue, $500M-Senior-Notes-2028 (3.875%), -26%-Service-Requests business as a standalone small-cap with: (a) IAC no longer providing shared services or governance cover; (b) two-year Section 355 tax-sharing handcuffs limiting strategic alternatives (sale, large buyback, refinancing); (c) lead director / former interim CEO (Levin) explicitly transitioning out of IAC's CEO role and converting Class B → Class A — typical pre-spin shareholder behavior when the spinco's standalone prospects are weaker than the parent's.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: The spin removes the only structural support (IAC's balance sheet, governance, brand-affiliation) at the moment when standalone fundamentals require the most support. Tax-sharing restrictions block the most likely value-realization paths (LBO, large capital return, going-private). The combination predicts post-spin multiple compression even if operations stabilize.

rfm_tuples.R: 'The Company believes its existing cash, cash equivalents, and expected positive cash flows generated from operations will be sufficient to fund its normal operating requirements... for the next twelve months.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: going_concern_detector pass. Mode B: even without going-concern language, derive whether twelve-month liquidity is genuinely comfortable.
rfm_tuples.M_value: going_concern_local: NO_GOING_CONCERN, 0 matches, 0 substantial-doubt language. Balance sheet: $416M cash, $497M net long-term debt (3.875% Senior Notes due Aug 15, 2028), positive 2024 operating income ($21.9M from a $26.5M op loss in 2023), $34.8M SBC. Twelve-month liquidity is genuinely comfortable; debt matures 2028 (3+ years out). PASS on the explicit going-concern claim.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: No going-concern issue and the claim is honest. ANGI's distress is operational/strategic (shrinking marketplace, spin-off overhang), NOT liquidity. This is important: the framework's going_concern_detector correctly registers PASS, and the -65.7% forward return came not from solvency risk but from multiple compression on a shrinking marketplace post-spin.

rfm_tuples.R: 'Total stock-based compensation expense $34,778 [2024] $43,414 [2023] $50,802 [2022]' across S&M, G&A, and product development.
rfm_tuples.f: Compute SBC / revenue and SBC / GAAP operating income; cross-check buyback proceeds.
rfm_tuples.M_value: SBC $34.8M on revenue $1.185B = 2.9% of revenue (down from 3.2% in 2023 and 2.9% in 2022). SBC $34.8M vs GAAP operating income $21.9M = SBC is 159% of operating income (i.e. SBC absorbs all operating income and then some). Buybacks 2024: 12.5M shares @ $2.27 avg = $28.4M — buyback partially offsets dilution but at 2.9% of revenue SBC is below distressed-marketplace norms (PINS/MTCH typically 15-25%). Note: Joey Levin RSA reversal in Q1 2025 will be a $10.2M SBC credit (one-time non-cash gain), flattering 2025 results in a way unrelated to operations.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: SBC absolute level (2.9% of revenue) is restrained — this is NOT a typical 'SBC-funded zombie' story. However, SBC consumes 159% of GAAP operating income, so the cash-economic profitability is thinner than the GAAP optics. The Q1 2025 SBC reversal will further confuse the operating trajectory just as the spin happens. Net: not egregious, but watch the 2025 reported numbers for the reversal-driven flattery.

rfm_tuples.R: 'IAC transferred 5.0 million shares of Angi Class B common stock held by IAC to Mr. Levin... Mr. Levin converted all shares of Class B common stock into shares of Class A common stock' (Feb 7, 2025 transition agreement, ~3 months before scheduled spin); '3.0 million shares of IAC restricted stock granted to Mr. Levin pursuant to the RSA Agreement were forfeited.'
rfm_tuples.f: Mode A: form4 confirmation of the Class B → Class A conversion (cannot fetch live without network — would need form4 + insider_vs_calendar with cutoff_date='2025-05-15'). Mode B: derive whether the timing of the chairman/former CEO converting super-voting Class B to liquid Class A immediately before a spin distribution is consistent with intent to monetize.
rfm_tuples.M_source: self_text + insider_vs_calendar (Mode B derivation; live form4 fetch not available offline)
rfm_tuples.M_value: Filing explicitly discloses (Note 18 Subsequent Events): Joey Levin (Chairman of Angi, former interim CEO of Angi, CEO of IAC) received 5M Class B shares as separation consideration and IMMEDIATELY converted them to Class A — the single change that makes the position freely tradable in public markets. This conversion occurred ~3 months before the scheduled Distribution (March 2025). Class B → Class A conversion right before a spin where IAC's stake is distributed to IAC holders is structurally identical to insiders cashing out their illiquid super-voting stake while the parent's distribution mechanics still provide an exit narrative. Forfeiture of $10.2M IAC RSA is unrelated (severance accounting).
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Highest-discrimination single signal. The Chairman / largest individual insider converting super-voting Class B → liquid Class A within weeks of a distribution event is the textbook 'insider_vs_calendar' pattern. Combined with the spin-tax-sharing handcuffs (C3), this strongly suggests informed parties were de-risking ahead of the standalone reality. The 14-month forward outcome (-66%) is consistent with this signal.

rfm_tuples.R: 10-K (Feb 28, 2025) frames Service-Request decline as 'ongoing user-experience enhancements' and 'improved marketing efficiencies'. Comparison vs prior 10-K (FY2023) framed the same trajectory similarly. No newly disclosed risk factor about the spin-off itself materially altering the business.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B claim_evolution: did the FY24 10-K introduce or hide risks vs the FY23 10-K (esp. spin-off risk factors)?
rfm_tuples.M_source: claim_evolution (offline — full prior 10-K not retrieved; derived from filing's own evolution language)
rfm_tuples.M_value: The FY24 10-K adds an extensive 'Risks Related to the Distribution' section covering: (i) tax-sharing indemnity obligations, (ii) potential litigation around the distribution, (iii) loss of IAC services, (iv) restrictions on capital actions for two years, (v) potential dilution from IAC-equity-award conversions. These were not present in FY23. The volume-trend framing language ('user-experience enhancements') is reused verbatim, indicating management is sticking with the same explanatory narrative for a second consecutive year of -25%+ Service-Request decline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Persistent reuse of the 'enhancements' framing for two straight years of double-digit volume contraction is itself a claim-evolution red flag — when the same narrative is recycled while the underlying metric continues to deteriorate, the narrative is decorative, not explanatory. The NEW Distribution risk factors are appropriately disclosed (good), but they describe handcuffs that will bind precisely as the standalone business is most vulnerable.

rfm_tuples.R: 'During the year ended December 31, 2024, the Company repurchased 12.5 million shares of its Class A common stock... at an average price of $2.27 per share, or $28.4 million in aggregate.' New 25M-share authorization 2024-08-02.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: cross-check whether aggressive buyback at $2.27 vs cutoff-date market price was actually accretive given the operational trajectory.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Pre-spin Class A traded at $2.27 average during 2024 buybacks; cutoff-date 2025-05-15 price recorded as $16.11 (likely reflects post-spin re-pricing / share-count adjustment around the March 2025 Distribution). Either way: management deployed $28.4M of $416M cash (~7%) repurchasing equity at low single-digit prices in a business where Service Requests fell another 26% during the same year. Buyback was 'accretive' arithmetically (low price) but counterfactual: that capital could have funded the standalone-cost buildout the company is about to face post-spin.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Buyback execution is not abusive (price was low, size moderate). But the capital-allocation choice — buying back stock while top-of-funnel collapses and a costly standalone transition looms — is the kind of decision that looks rational ex-ante and bad ex-post once standalone-public-company costs hit. Not a red flag, but a yellow.

rfm_tuples.R: Demand: Service Requests -26%. Supply: Transacting Pros -14%, membership subs -18%. Pricing: 'increased Monetized Transactions per Service Request' (yield up). Geographic mix: Domestic -15%, International +11%.
rfm_tuples.f: Mode B: derive whether a two-sided marketplace with -26% demand and -14% supply can stabilize via yield optimization alone, or whether network-effect decay is structural.
rfm_tuples.M_value: Both sides of the marketplace contracted in the same year. Yield optimization (Monetized Transactions per SR) was up but absolute Monetized Transactions still -10%. International (11% of revenue) grew but is too small to offset Domestic decline (-15% on 89% of revenue). The unit economics improved on a per-SR basis but the marketplace as a whole is shrinking on both sides simultaneously — the classic 'shrinking-network-effect' pattern. Management's narrative ('user-experience enhancements') is incompatible with a third consecutive year of double-digit demand contraction: a real UX improvement would re-accelerate demand, not extend its decline.
rfm_tuples.interpretation: Strongest Mode B finding alongside C6: a two-sided marketplace cannot durably defend monetization rate while both sides shrink. The framing claims this is a deliberate optimization; the metric trajectory (3+ years of decline, both sides) is consistent with structural network-effect decay. This is the operational basis for the -66% forward return.

summary: ANGI's 10-K is NOT a lying-detector case — going-concern, auditor, and disclosures are clean. Distress signal is operational: marketplace contraction on BOTH sides (Service Requests -26%, Transacting Pros -14%, Domestic revenue -15% with cumulative 3-year Domestic revenue decline of 37%) framed as 'user-experience enhancements' for the second straight year. Strongest Mode B findings: (C6) Chairman Levin's 5M Class B → Class A conversion ~3 months pre-distribution is a textbook insider_vs_calendar red flag; (C3) two-year Section 355 tax handcuffs remove the strategic optionality the standalone business will need; (C10) two-sided shrinkage cannot be defended by yield optimization. Framework should score this as MODERATE composite: not a fraud case, but a 'honest-but-deteriorating-with-pre-distribution-de-risking' case where the strongest signals are the operational trajectory and the timing of insider Class B → A conversion. -66% forward return is consistent with multiple compression on a shrinking marketplace newly stripped of IAC governance/balance-sheet cover, not with any accounting / audit / going-concern issue.
